facts.about: Incorporated in 2010, Eternal Limited (previously Zomato Limited) is one of the leading online Food Service platforms in terms of the value of food sold. Its offerings include food delivery, dining-out services, Loyalty programs, and others. As of December 31, 2020, Eternal has established a strong footprint across 23 countries with 131,233 active food delivery restaurants, 161,637 active delivery partners, and an average monthly food order of 10.7 million customers.

flags.text: Operating margin expanded 19 pts in 3 years (-17% → 2.2%)
Operating cash flow was negative over 5 years (₹49 cr) despite ₹-949 cr of profit
Latest quarter growth (+78%) well below 3-yr trend (+97%)

business.summary: Eternal Ltd. is a technology platform services provider operating in food delivery, quick commerce, B2B supplies, and going-out segments. It generates revenue through commissions, inventory-led sales, and service fees.

segments.name: India food ordering and delivery
segments.note: Revenue grew 26% YoY driven by higher order volumes and revenue per order.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.note: Revenue grew 626% YoY due to shift to an inventory-led model.

segments.name: Going-out
segments.note: Revenue grew 32% YoY driven by dining-out, movies, and events.

segments.name: B2B supplies
segments.note: Revenue declined 13% YoY due to scaling down non-restaurant business.

guidance.statement: Over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish.
guidance.quote: It's hard to project or comment on margin trajectory every quarter but broadly, over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish.

guidance.statement: We maintain that guidance as of now.
guidance.quote: It's very early on that three-year journey; we're still two quarters in, so I don't want to jump too much into the future. We maintain that guidance as of now.

guidance.statement: We expect NOV growth to pick up starting the December quarter on a YoY basis.
guidance.quote: That's right. ... We're talking about NOV growth pickup starting the December quarter on a YoY basis?

guidance.statement: We think at this point we're likely to end at the higher end of the range.
guidance.quote: We think at this point we're likely to end at the higher end of the range that we had guided earlier and hence, the communication.

guidance.statement: We are targeting a long-term GAAP EBIT margin of 4%.
guidance.quote: And then you get to a GAAP EBIT margin of 4% as long-term?

guidance.statement: We expect capex per store to be lower than INR 2.5 crore going forward.
guidance.quote: If you therefore look at our capex over the last six months, nine months or a longer period, and the capex per store for that period, you will find it is lower than INR 2.5 crore. We expect that to continue going forward.

guidance.statement: We estimate a steady-state net working capital of 12 days.
guidance.quote: The 12 days that we are saying here is a steady-state estimate right now.

guidance.statement: We are on track on our guidance for March of 3,000 stores.
guidance.quote: On store addition, we're on track on our guidance for March of 3,000 stores.

guidance.statement: We have given overall guidance of 60% CAGR for quick commerce.
guidance.quote: We've given overall guidance of 60% CAGR and that would obviously mean some reasonable store expansion, but we're not planning to give out any specific number guidance on that.

guidance.statement: As we move to 5-6% margin that we are saying we will get to at some point.
guidance.quote: As we move to 5-6% margin that we are saying we will get to at some point, contribution margin will go up and on a year-on-year basis, we'll see that trend consistently.

guidance.statement: We have extremely high confidence in the business model to deliver 5% to 6% of NOV margins.
guidance.quote: In the long term, in our letter we have mentioned that our confidence on margins going to 5% to 6% of NOV remains high

guidance.statement: We now expect the losses to come down sequentially from here towards breakeven in the next 4-6 quarters.
guidance.quote: Irrespective of that, as we have mentioned in question 13, we now expect the losses to come down sequentially from here towards breakeven in the next four to six quarters.

guidance.statement: The ROCE outcome should still be north of 40%.
guidance.quote: and hence, as a consequence of that, the ROCE outcome should still be north of 40%. That's what we're solving for.

guidance.statement: We expect year-on-year growth to continue slowly trending up towards 20% YoY.
guidance.quote: As of now, as we have mentioned, we expect year-on-year growth to continue slowly trending up towards 20% YoY, is what our current sense on the market is.

scorecard.promised: Maintain a 60% CAGR for quick commerce over the next three years.
scorecard.delivered: Revenue grew 77.6% YoY in Sep 2026, down from 182% in Jun 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Annual revenue surged from ₹12,114 cr in Mar 2024 to ₹54,364 cr in Mar 2026, exceeding the 60% target.

scorecard.promised: Targeting 5% to 6% long-term; flattish over the next 1-2 years.
scorecard.delivered: Operating margin reached 3.1% in Sep 2026, up from 1.2% in Mar 2025.
scorecard.evidence: Margins improved from 1.2% to 3.1% over six quarters, but remain below the 5-6% long-term goal.

scorecard.promised: On track to reach 3,000 stores by March.
scorecard.delivered: Management maintains guidance for 3,000 stores by March 2027.
scorecard.evidence: Current store count not disclosed in numbers, but management reaffirmed the March target in recent calls.

scorecard.promised: Expect year-on-year growth to trend up towards 20% YoY.
scorecard.delivered: Overall revenue growth was 77.6% in Sep 2026, well above the 20% floor.
scorecard.evidence: Consolidated revenue growth has stayed above 60% for nine consecutive quarters.

scorecard.promised: Estimate a steady-state net working capital of 12 days.
scorecard.delivered: Debtor days stood at 12 days as of Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: The balance sheet shows debtor days exactly matching the 12-day steady-state estimate.

narrative.scoreline: Management has successfully scaled revenue and improved margins from negative territory, though growth is decelerating as they approach long-term profitability targets.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Inventory losses are asymptotic and have stabilized at 1.8% of NOV.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Operating margins have expanded from 1.2% to 3.1% since Mar 2025, supporting the stabilization narrative.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Capex per store will be lower than INR 2.5 crore going forward.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: FCF was negative ₹1,114 cr in Mar 2026 despite positive PAT, suggesting heavy capital intensity.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Going-out losses will reach breakeven within 4-6 quarters from Q3 FY26.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Consolidated PAT has remained positive for nine consecutive quarters, reaching ₹125 cr in Sep 2026.

bull: Revenue grew from ₹12,114 cr to ₹54,364 cr in two years, far exceeding the 60% CAGR target.
Operating margins expanded 19 percentage points over three years, reaching 3.1% in the latest quarter.
The company maintains a strong balance sheet with ₹31,275 cr net worth and low 0.18x debt-to-equity.
bear: Free Cash Flow remains deeply negative at -₹1,114 cr for FY26, despite reported accounting profits.
Revenue growth slowed sharply to 77.6% in Sep 2026 from 182% in the prior quarter.
Cash conversion cycle has deteriorated to 2 days from a much more favorable -132 days three years ago.
watch: Check if Sep 2026 margin of 3.1% holds steady toward the 5-6% long-term target.

claims.claim: We want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth to drive the growth upwards.
claims.quote: Directionally, we want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth as much as it makes sense to continue to drive the growth upwards.

claims.claim: The bulk of new store expansion will be in smaller cities, where paybacks are extremely good.
claims.quote: Directionally, we've also mentioned in the letter that the bulk of the expansion of these new stores will be in smaller cities. We do expect that to be the focus from here on.

claims.claim: Costs are currently carved out in the 'Others' segment and are not meaningful at this stage.
claims.quote: They're not very meaningful at this stage, and we don't expect the capex or cost to become meaningful, at least as of now, unless, of course, we receive a blockbuster response.

claims.claim: Competition is more predictable now, providing an opportunity to become more aggressive on infrastructure expansion.
claims.quote: But now, as we mentioned last time also, competition is more predictable now, and that provides an opportunity for us to become more aggressive on infrastructure expansion.

claims.claim: Discount-led growth is not sustainable and we expect this to not continue beyond the near future.
claims.quote: We expect this to not continue beyond the near future so we do think that this will come off.

claims.claim: We do not expect NAOV to grow from here; it should remain in the same range.
claims.quote: Generally, Aditya, we're not expecting the NAOV to grow from here. If you look at year-on-year, it's flat.

claims.claim: Inventory losses are at 1.8% of NOV and have been fairly asymptotic.
claims.quote: It has been fairly asymptotic so far. We don't expect it to be materially much better.

claims.claim: We are adding about 10 kitchens per quarter and will be cautiously expanding for now.
claims.quote: Broadly, we are adding about 10-odd kitchens in a quarter, that's the pace of expansion there.

claims.claim: Growth is driven by assortment expansion, geographical expansion, and demand densification in existing and new cities.
claims.quote: It's a function of assortment expansion, geographical expansion as well as more demand densification in the cities where we are present today and we might also get into newer cities.

claims.claim: We continue to see value in keeping marketing spends high due to low customer acquisition costs.
claims.quote: We feel a lot of our competitors in the market have pulled back on this so we're seeing extremely low cost of customer acquisition and we, therefore, continue to see value in keeping marketing spends high at this point.

claims.claim: We optimize for absolute profit rather than profit margin percentage.
claims.quote: the objective is to optimize for growth of absolute profit and not the profit margin percentage.

claims.claim: The dip in store throughput is a function of assortment expansion, which we do not see as a concern.
claims.quote: As I mentioned, a lot of our store additions, not just last quarter but last two, three quarters, has been towards assortment expansion and as we now further expand assortment, the turnover of this long tail is not as high

claims.claim: Competitive intensity is volatile and impacts our margins, top-line growth, and store expansion plans.
claims.quote: Overall, there's definitely an impact of competition and it impacts our margins, it impacts our top-line growth, it impacts our store expansion plans and various other things.

claims.claim: Capex per store will increase due to warehousing infrastructure expansion and investment in automation.
claims.quote: It tends to be chunky, and we make a lot of investment in the warehousing infrastructure as well, especially as we expand deeper and deeper into the country. That would explain the increase in capex per store.

risks.text: Company faces uncertainty regarding GST orders received from authorities in respect of delivery charges.
Climate change risks, including extreme weather, may impact last-mile food deliveries and customer experience.
Investments in other entities involve significant estimates and judgment in determining fair value.
Impairment assessment of goodwill involves significant estimates regarding future revenue growth and valuation assumptions.
